objective: Translate the complete 23-part canonical CIN source ZTF-CIN-ARCH-001 v1.0.0 into repository architecture, feasibility assessment, logical contracts, LC-01 pilot protocol, participation strategy, governance/risk specification, staged roadmap, handbook, product architecture, API and scientific-validation boundaries, README and cumulative knowledge while preserving ZTF scientific baselines and subsystem independence.
previous_knowledge_consumed: ZTF Classifier v1.0.1 is a published immutable Python package; the frozen scientific baseline v0.2.0 is a separate immutable model/benchmark identity.
The repository already has observation, catalog-context, discovery-candidate, human-review/feedback, model-provenance, FastAPI, Workbench and scientific-validation boundaries.
CatalogMatch/CatalogContext preserve contextual cross-match evidence but do not provide a complete canonical identity registry; AOIC remains a separate proposed workstream.
CIN is specified as a logically independent, optional human-in-the-loop subsystem. Local ZTF analysis, inference, benchmark evaluation and reports must continue if CIN is unavailable.
Human consensus is not ground truth; novelty is not discovery; human contributions must not contaminate the protected benchmark or trigger automatic production retraining.
Active-learning selection must retain random audits and representative samples to evaluate selection bias.
The canonical CIN source contains 23 parts and proposes staged implementation from feasibility audit through controlled LC-01 pilot and later task families.

Existing discovery and human-review interfaces could be mistaken for a complete citizen-science annotation system unless the missing task, contribution, consensus, quality and dataset-release lifecycles are documented.
unresolved: Detailed route, persistence, authentication, authorization, job and UI audit remains.
Image-source availability, cutout provenance, licensing and data-retention feasibility remain.
Privacy notice, consent, deletion, pseudonymization, threat model and attribution policy remain.
Pilot sample size, control adjudication, assignment count, metrics and stopping rules remain to be selected from evidence.
No runtime CIN implementation or scientific pilot has been executed.

findings: CIN must remain an optional and logically independent subsystem.
Raw human responses, QC states, aggregates, expert reviews and research-ready annotations require separate provenance and lifecycle states.
Consensus is not ground truth; novelty is not discovery; human annotations do not automatically retrain the production model.
A controlled LC-01 pilot is the first recommended experiment; a public contributor network is not required to establish feasibility.
CIN task references must preserve original survey IDs and unresolved identity until AOIC is accepted and evidence-backed.

open_blockers: No CIN runtime tests exist in this documentation-only cycle.
CI result for the exact final PR head must be inspected before merge.
No scientific validation or pilot result is available.

knowledge_carried_forward: Treat ZTF-CIN-ARCH-001 v1.0.0 as the canonical proposed CIN source.
Keep CIN, AOIC and the ZTF computational core as separate systems with versioned contracts.
Start with feasibility, contracts and controlled LC-01 pilot; do not implement the entire network at once.
Keep human consensus, expert review and scientific validation distinct.
Do not increase platform progress or scientific readiness based on documentation and planning.
Product activity metrics must remain separate from scientific and operational metrics; recognition is optional and cannot imply scientific credentials.
Institutional claims must describe CIN as proposed/planned until the relevant capability and evidence exist.
